mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 5.0% indicates a restrictive monetary policy stance that increases the cost of capital for corporations, leading to lower equity valuations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both monthly employment (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based economic contraction that reduces corporate revenue growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances when PAYEMS and HOUST both decline, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5% for two consecutive months), an increase in the federal funds rate compresses corporate profit margins and raises discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in less than 40% of instances during monetary tightening cycles, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level below 1500 thousand units indicates weak residential demand, which reduces construction sector activity and consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances when HOUST < 1500, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production below 100 (index 2017=100) signals a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in year-over-year CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% and a stable or rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an inflationary environment that prompts the Fed to tighten policy, reducing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY and FEDFUNDS stable/rising, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a housing market recovery (defined by HOUST rising above 1600 thousand units for two consecutive months), increased residential construction activity boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in less than 40% of instances during housing market recoveries, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
